Single SOT-23-5 op-amps vary in pin ordering across vendors; verify Pin 1–5.
A part wins only if its recommended Vs range strictly encompasses the counterpart on both ends.
Exceeding Vs,abs causes immediate gate-oxide or junction breakdown.

CMOS/JFET pA-class inputs avoid offset voltage drops across high-impedance (>100 kΩ) sensors.
Multiply by channel count for total IC standby current draw.
RRIO prevents clipping on low-voltage 3.3 V single-supply ADC buffers.

swap_risks: HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: LM2904DR has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (26 V, p.4) than LM358DR (32 V, p.4); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 26 V.

HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (LM2904DR: -40..125 °C Extended Industrial / Automotive Temp (-40°C to +125°C TA) vs LM358DR: 0..70 °C Commercial (0°C to 70°C)); LM358DR cold limit only 0 °C, LM358DR hot limit only 70 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
engineering_verdict: LM2904DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and LM358DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because Vs,abs,max drops >=15% (26 V vs 32 V); ambient temperature grade differs (-40..125 °C vs 0..70 °C). Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 0.7 MHz (p.11) vs 0.7 MHz (p.10), supply ceiling 26 V (p.5) vs 30 V (p.5), Vos 7 mV (p.11) vs 7 mV (p.10), Ib 1x gap (20000 vs 20000 pA), voltage noise 40 vs 40 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM2904DR "Hidden 26 V Supply Ceiling Trap When Swapping From 30 V/32 V LM358DR to 'Extended-Temp' LM2904DR!" (p.4) and LM358DR "Non-Rail-to-Rail Upper Input and Output Headroom Ceiling" (p.10). BOM decision: Choose LM2904DR when matching your existing Texas Instruments SOIC-8 (D (8-Pin SOIC)) qualification and -40..125 °C grade; choose LM358DR when supply rails exceed 26 V (rated up to 30 V). Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
